title: Exposing CHEATERS In the Caro-Kann Defense: Fantasy Variation | GM Naroditsky’s Top Theory Speedrun

moves.spoken: We take White and face the Caro-Kann.
We build the centre with d4.
Black challenges with d5.
We play f3 — the Fantasy Variation, sharp and tactical, and far less studied than the mainlines.
Black plays e6 — the most reputable reply — and we treat it like a French. Note the threat: ...dxe4 and then ...Qh4 with check.
We defend while developing — the knight to c3 reinforces e4 and takes the sting out of ...Qh4, which would now meet g3.
Black pins with the bishop to b4 — the main move, just like the Winawer French.
We try a3 — a pawn sacrifice, forcing the bishop to decide.
Black takes on c3 with check.
We recapture with the b-pawn onto c3. Black has given up the dark-squared bishop, leaving a position riddled with dark-square weaknesses on d6 and e7.
Black grabs on e4.
The computer move — not a bishop but the knight to h3. It prepares fxe4 to win the pawn back, and a check on h4 is now harmless because Nf2 would cover e4.
Black plays the theory move to a5, the queen eyeing the c3-pawn.
We fianchetto to b2 rather than d2 — d2 would run into ...e3, deflecting the bishop and forcing our king to move. On b2 it looks bad now, but c4 and d5 later give it real potential energy.
Black develops the knight to f6.
We take back on e4.
Black recaptures with the knight — dubious, I think.
We develop the bishop to d3, hitting the knight and preparing to castle. If ...Nxc3, then Qd2 would pin and win it, since the a5-queen is undefended.
Black drops the knight back to f6.
We castle — king to safety, and more importantly the rook lands on the semi-open f-file, a hallmark of the Fantasy.
Black plays the slow b6, preparing to fianchetto — but we're a couple of moves from smashing open the kingside.
On theme, we push c4 — investing a tempo to free the b2-bishop and prepare d5.
Black connects the knights with ...Nbd7, taking the sting out of d5.
We bring the queen into the attack with Qf3; Black develops the bishop to b7; and the queen slides to g3 — its real destination, bearing down the g-file at g7 and clear of the rook.
Black castles queenside, conceding g7 — not an easy thing to do, but the grandmaster choice.
We take the free pawn — even in attack, material matters; the queen crashes into g7.
Black swings the rook to g8, hitting the queen.
The queen slips out to f7, grabbing a second pawn; Black answers with the quiet rook to e8 — a high-level defensive resource.
